absent: PMU MSR read and write validation, counter emulation, overflow handling and PMI injection beyond refresh, init and mediated paths.
Host capability discovery, branch compatibility predicate, and performance capability register layout internals.
Posted descriptor and pending-bitmap layout, suppress-notification semantics, and wakeup-list insertion and removal lifecycle.
Virtual ECREATE and EINIT fault classification, EPC interaction, and launch-key verification internals.
ENCLS dispatch outside creation and initialization, including SGX2 augmentation and modification leaves.
Guest CPUID construction for performance and SGX leaves and guest-supported extended-feature negotiation.

findings.text: Provides the Intel PMU operation vector consumed by generic KVM PMU logic, covering PMC index translation, MSR validity plus read and write, lifecycle refresh plus init plus reset plus cleanup, PMI delivery, mediated mode support probe plus load plus put, and global control programming. Also publishes counter limits and register bases used by callers.

Fixed counter positions have a stable architectural meaning: position zero counts retired instructions, position one counts core cycles, position two counts reference cycles. The mapping is resolved through host perf configuration at init time and a missing host encoding for an advertised fixed counter is treated as a warnable inconsistency, yielding a zero configuration.

PMU refresh initializes derived guest state from CPUID and host capabilities in order: clear branch records, reject use while branch passthrough is active or after the vCPU ran, parse virtualization leaves for version and counter counts, apply host capability ceilings, then program masks, branch presence, fixed counters, reserved global bits and precise-event policy. Version zero stops early and version one stops before fixed-counter handling.

Guest visible PMU limits never exceed host limits: general and fixed counts, counter widths, event mask length and available event types are each truncated to host capability values. Reserved global control bits mark unimplemented general and fixed positions as unavailable, status reserves additionally permit buffer, state-change and optionally trace notifications, and precise-event reserves follow either counter availability or baseline versus legacy format policy.

PMU init creates per-vCPU counter descriptors before any guest use: general slots receive sequential indexes and fixed slots receive indexes offset into the fixed range, each bound to its vCPU with cleared runtime configuration, while fixed slots also cache their architectural event encoding. Branch bookkeeping starts empty with no active host event and no passthrough.

PMI handling only affects branch control when guest branch use is active. For intermediate architectural versions newer than one and older than four, a guest request to freeze branch records on PMI causes the hypervisor to clear the branch-recording enable while preserving the freeze request, matching legacy hardware behavior.

Reset unconditionally drops any guest branch host event. Cleanup drops it conditionally, retaining the event only while the guest still has branch recording enabled in its debug control view, so host resources are not held after the guest disables the feature.

Mediated PMU use requires a host PMU version of at least four, host full-width counter write support read through the performance capabilities register when the platform exposes it, and VMCS support for loading global control. Missing requirements mean no mediation; missing VMCS acceleration on capable hardware is treated as a warnable inconsistency.

On guest entry the mediated path reconciles overflow status by clearing newly set host bits and setting newly set guest bits, then loads the guest fixed-counter control value into hardware. On exit it saves hardware status into the vCPU record, clears non-zero hardware status, and clears non-zero hardware fixed-counter control. Global control itself is programmed through a dedicated VMCS field and is already preserved at exit.

The per-vCPU branch-record descriptor holds a record set describing count and capabilities, an optional host perf event used for passthrough emulation, and a flag recording whether branch MSRs are currently unintercepted. Records may be imprecise if the host reclaims branch hardware while passthrough is active.

Posted-interrupt wakeups use a per-CPU list of vCPUs plus a per-CPU raw spinlock. The wakeup scan holds the local lock for the whole traversal. A dedicated nesting level is defined for taking this lock while scheduling out, preventing lock-order complaints.

Wakeup handling runs on the current CPU, walks that CPU wakeup list under its lock, tests the posted descriptor notification flag for each entry, and wakes only entries with the flag set. It performs no other state mutation.

Before APIC virtualization state restore the posted descriptor notification is cleared and its pending vector bitmap is zeroed. A pending posted interrupt is reported when notification is set, or when suppression is set while the pending bitmap is non-empty.

Bypass start requests an unblock kick on every CPU for the VM after checking platform support. Interrupt remapping update binds a host IRQ either to a target vCPU posted descriptor physical address plus vector, or detaches it when no target is supplied.

Conversion from the VT-specific vCPU extension to the generic vCPU structure goes through the enclosing VMX vCPU container, so the generic pointer is derived by containing-structure arithmetic rather than a stored back pointer.

Intel PMU register ABI: general event selectors start at the P6 selector base, general counters at the PMC base, fixed counters at the fixed-counter base, global control is the core global control register, consecutive registers are spaced by one, minimum general counter count is one.

ENCLS operand sizes and alignments: creation page info uses 32 bytes aligned to 32, creation destination and creation content use 4096 aligned to 4096, creation metadata uses 64 aligned to 64, initialization signature uses 1808 aligned to 4096, initialization destination uses 4096 aligned to 4096, initialization token uses 304 aligned to 512.

ENCLS guest addresses start from the supplied offset plus data-segment base outside 64-bit mode, then require the requested alignment. In 64-bit mode untagging plus canonical-form checking applies; outside 64-bit mode segment usability, writable data type, limit containment and wraparound are checked with 32-bit truncation. Any failure injects a general protection fault and aborts the leaf.

Guest virtual operands are translated for the intended direction and a failed translation injects an emulated page fault and resumes the guest. Guest physical values are converted to host virtual addresses with page offset preserved and invalid mappings exit to userspace with an emulation-failure record. Host memory reads that fault also exit to userspace with address and length recorded.

Creation handling deep-copies page info from the guest, validates and translates metadata, content and destination pointers through virtual to physical to host stages, snapshots the enclave control structure into a kernel page, enforces provisioning-key permission plus CPUID miscselect plus attribute plus extended-feature plus size ceilings including mandatory FP and SSE coverage, then invokes the virtual creation primitive and either skips the guest instruction, injects a mapped fault, or returns the host error.

Initialization handling translates signature, destination and token pointers without crossing pages, invokes the virtual init primitive with the VM launch public-key hash, maps host faults to either an SGX present-write page fault at the destination or a general protection fault based on host and guest SGX2 support, and on success updates status flags with carry, parity, adjust, sign and overflow cleared and zero flag plus accumulator reflecting the primitive result before skipping the guest instruction.
Creation through tracking leaves are always permitted once ENCLS is reachable. Augmentation through type-change leaves require guest SGX2 support; all other leaf numbers are rejected.
Guest virtual to guest physical reads select user privilege only when the current privilege level is three, otherwise supervisor privilege, then delegate to the vCPU address-translation walker.

Three hazards are mitigated: PMU refresh must not run after the vCPU executed or while branch passthrough is active; hardware fixed-counter control is cleared on mediated exit to avoid leaking guest settings or enabling counters in the host; enclave creation copies guest control data into kernel memory before validation to prevent concurrent guest modification from bypassing permission checks.
SGX virtualization defaults to enabled through a mostly-read global switch, and the launch enclave public-key hash is held as four host words marked read-only after init.
VMX PMU, posted-interrupt and SGX components prefix kernel log messages with the module name, and their private headers use include guards to prevent multiple inclusion.
